title: SharpRelativeErrorSmoothConvex.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained differentiable convex objectives on a real Hilbert space, satisfying the global quadratic upper model with L>0. A minimizer exists within distance R≥0 of x0.

oracle.label: inexact_gradient
oracle.details: Queries and replies are Hilbert-space vectors. Every reply g at x satisfies ‖g−∇f(x)‖≤α‖∇f(x)‖ for every history and oracle seed. No function values, independence, or unbiasedness are required.

distinctive_assumptions.label: relative_error
distinctive_assumptions.details: Public parameters include L,x0,α,R,ε and the Hilbert space. With Q=2+LR²/ε, validity requires 0≤α<1 and α≤1/[100(33(1+log Q))¹²]. Errors may depend arbitrarily on query history, subject to the pointwise relative bound.

distinctive_assumptions.label: non_euclidean_geometry
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is an arbitrary complete real inner-product space; finite dimension is not required.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothAndConvex.lean: Public.E, Public.innerProductSpace via linearE, Public.completeE

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: For ε>0, the returned point must satisfy f(output)−f(xstar)≤ε for a global minimizer xstar.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The objective-gap requirement holds almost surely under the product of the algorithm seed law and the oracle seed law, within the fixed oracle budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: Smooth convex minimization uses a pointwise relative-error gradient oracle with arbitrary history dependence and an accuracy-dependent polylogarithmic restriction on its public error parameter.

descriptionHtml:
Sharp Relative-Error Convex Optimization

We consider minimizing a differentiable convex function f:E→R on a real Hilbert space E. The function is L-smooth, with L>0, and a given point x0∈E is within distance R≥0 of a global minimizer x⋆. At x∈E, the oracle returns a vector g∈E satisfying ∥g−∇f(x)∥≤α∥∇f(x)∥, where α≥0 obeys a stringent accuracy-dependent bound. For tolerance ε>0, the goal is an output x¯∈E satisfying f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under P, the joint law of algorithm and oracle randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E. The algorithm receives E, L, x0, α, R, and ε. The parameters satisfy L>0,R≥0,ε>0,0≤α<1,α≤1100[33(1+log⁡(2+LR2/ε))]12, where log denotes the natural logarithm.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity and smoothness). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere on E. For every x,y∈E, f(y)≥f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩,f(y)≤f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+L2∥y−x∥2.

Assumption 2 (Initial distance). There exists x⋆∈E such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈E,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R.

Assumption 3 (Uniform relative error). Queries may be made at any point of E. The relative-error inequality stated above holds for every query history, every query point, and every realization of the oracle randomness. Oracle replies may depend on the preceding queries and replies, and the oracle randomness may be dependent across calls. Algorithm randomness is independent of oracle randomness.

After the allotted oracle calls, the output must satisfy f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤εP-a.s. Here x⋆ is a fixed global minimizer, independent of the randomness.

comparisonHtml:
Convex differentiable f on a real Hilbert space satisfies f(y)≤f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+L2∥y−x∥2, with L>0 and a minimizer x⋆ satisfying ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R, R≥0. Every oracle reply obeys ∥g−∇f(x)∥≤α∥∇f(x)∥, with 0≤α≤α⋆=[100(33(1+log⁡(2+LR2/ε)))12]−1. Target: f(xout)−f(x⋆)≤ε, ε>0, for every admissible reply sequence. The setup imposes no algorithm restriction.

import LongTails.Setups.RelativeErrorSmoothConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Basic

namespace LongTails.Setups.SharpRelativeErrorSmoothConvex

abbrev Public := RelativeErrorSmoothConvex.Public

abbrev spec : OracleTemplate.Setup :=
  { RelativeErrorSmoothConvex.spec with
    valid := fun p => RelativeErrorSmoothConvex.spec.valid p ∧
      p.α ≤ 1 / (100 * (33 * (1 + Real.log (2 + p.L * p.R ^ 2 / p.ε))) ^ 12) }

end LongTails.Setups.SharpRelativeErrorSmoothConvex
